narrative: Material PL1__M4174A5C exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.32) across 95 working days with a slight decreasing trend, and highly variable lead times (CV=0.44, range 0.78–5.94 days). Lead time variance dominates the demand-during-lead-time uncertainty, making safety stock the critical lever. The SAP baseline holds zero safety stock and orders at MOQ (80,084) far more frequently than optimal; the recommended (r,Q) policy raises order size to the EOQ of 497,220 units, cuts annual orders from 81.6 to 13.1, and introduces 52,369 units of safety stock to meet the 95% service level — delivering a 65% total cost reduction.
warnings: Lead time anomalies (3 near-zero observations < 0.1 days) removed before statistics
EOQ order quantity (497,220) consumes 75% of max storage — monitor for demand growth

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review reorder-point policy with EOQ
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous with no zero-demand days and moderate variability; unit cost is low but volume is high, making ordering cost the dominant driver. EOQ-based (r,Q) minimises total inventory cost while the reorder point provides the required 95% service level protection against combined demand and lead time uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The recommended order quantity (497,220) plus safety stock (52,369) totals 549,589 units — 75% of max storage (732,500). This leaves a 182,911-unit buffer. If mean demand grows or lead time variability worsens, the EOQ could breach capacity; a quarterly review of the EOQ is recommended.
